# Test data

The verification corpus (architecture section 12, verification plan section 8). Every file records where it came from and its licence, so the corpus stays redistributable.

## Size policy

Decided in work breakdown slice 0 (decision record 0004) and checked by `cargo xtask testdata`:

- No file above 1 MiB, and no more than 20 MiB in total.
- Generate shapes procedurally where possible. The analytic oracle parts (cylinder, cone, sphere, helical groove, ruled surface) and the 1M-triangle benchmark model are generated by `openchuck-testkit::parts`, so they are not stored here.
- Golden files are plain text, so a review shows a real diff.
- If a real model ever needs to exceed the limits, raise it first: Git LFS or a separate test-data repository is still an open decision (architecture section 13).

| `stl/*.stl` | Written by `stl/generate.py` for this repository (slice 2, decision record 0010) | AGPL-3.0-or-later, as part of this repository | The STL corpus for IMP-01, IMP-03, IMP-04 and NFR-07, and the seed corpus of the `stl_import` fuzz target. A 10 mm cube with outward triangles as `cube_ascii.stl`, `cube_binary.stl`, `cube_binary_solid_header.stl` (binary whose header starts with `solid`) and `cube_nameless_crlf.stl` (a bare `solid` line, Windows line endings). Units: `cube_inch.stl` (a 1 in cube, `units=in` on the `solid` line), `cube_metre_binary.stl` (a 0.5 m cube, `UNITS=m` in the header), `cube_unknown_unit.stl` (`units=furlong`); for the size check, `cube_small.stl` (a 1-unit cube), `cube_speck_binary.stl` (0.05 units) and `cube_huge.stl` (5000 units). `two_cubes.stl`: two solids in one file. One defect each: `defect_hole.stl` (a facet missing), `defect_flipped.stl` (facet 6 wound backwards, normal to match), `defect_normal.stl` (facet 4's stated normal reversed), `defect_inside_out.stl` (binary, every facet reversed), `defect_non_manifold.stl` (a fin on one edge), `defect_degenerate.stl` (a facet with three equal corners). Damaged: `broken_empty.stl`, `broken_garbage.stl` (40 bytes), `broken_truncated_binary.stl`, `broken_truncated_ascii.stl`, `broken_bad_number.stl`, `broken_bad_keyword.stl`, `broken_nan_binary.stl`, `broken_no_triangles.stl`. Regenerate with `python3 testdata/stl/generate.py testdata/stl`. `.gitattributes` keeps them byte-exact. |
| `stl/blisk.stl` | Designed in OpenSCAD by the project owner in an earlier session; converted from OpenSCAD's ASCII output (1,195,782 bytes) to binary STL (319,384 bytes) to stay under the 1 MiB file limit, with the same 6,386 facets and normals (OpenSCAD wrote six significant digits, which a 32-bit float holds) | AGPL-3.0-or-later, as part of this repository (contributed by the project owner) | A single closed bladed disk: 40 mm in diameter, 50 mm long along X (the rotary axis), 6,386 triangles, volume 35,419 mm3; `openchuck-cli inspect` finds no problems. The model the owner used for the frame-time benchmark on the laptop (OI-264), and a sample project for slice 20 item 6 (the owner's decision on OI-311, 17 Oct 2026). It is a real part, unlike the generated reference parts. |
| `tools/library/`, `tools/broken/`, `tools/profiles/` | Written by hand for this repository (slice 4, decision record 0014) | AGPL-3.0-or-later, as part of this repository | The tool library and custom profile corpus for TL-01, TL-03, TL-11 and NFR-07, and the seed corpora of the `tool_library_toml` and `tool_profile_toml` fuzz targets. `library/` is a sample library folder with one tool file of every type (flat, ball, bull-nose, tapered ball, V-bit, chamfer, drill, custom corner rounder) and `tool-sets/makera-z1.toml`, a sample Z1 tool set (illustrative numbers, not the machine's tool changer layout); cutting data are plausible corpus values, not recommendations. `broken/`: damaged tool files (`corner_radius`, `undercut_profile`, `truncated`, `tool_number`, `stepover`) and tool sets (`tool_set_duplicate_number`, `tool_set_number_zero`). Profiles: `corner_rounder.toml` (arc by radius, concave), `ball_two_arcs.toml` (a 6 mm ball as two arcs, by centre and by radius); damaged: `broken_undercut.toml`, `broken_half_circle.toml`, `broken_arc_both_forms.toml`, `broken_nan.toml`, `broken_syntax.toml`. |
| `golden/helical_cone.txt` | Written by `cargo test -p openchuck-path --test helical` with `OPENCHUCK_BLESS=1` (slice 5, decision record 0018) | AGPL-3.0-or-later, as part of this repository | The golden toolpath of helical finishing on a small generated cone (NFR-08): every move at six decimals, no negative zero. The subset file holds every code a rotary post is expected to emit and LinuxCNC 2.9.10's `rs274` reads it without error. The extra file must give errors naming the feature, never a silent misread. |
